title: Per-Node Activation Function Evolution in Indirectly Encoded Substrates: Solvability, Limits, and Emergent Diversity
abstract: arXiv:2610.00149v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Biological neurons achieve computational diversity through specialized types: tonic, bursting, adapting, and fast-spiking cells coexist within the same circuit. Artificial neural networks, by contrast, apply a single activation function uniformly to all nodes, which limits what they can represent. We show that this uniformity creates hard limits for evolutionary search: across sparse evolved substrates, monotonic functions fail to solve parity beyond its smallest instance, XOR, while a single oscillatory unit suffices at all tested scales. The gap is one of search and sparsity, not representation: monotonic networks can represent parity with a modest number of hidden units, and gradient descent recovers that solution. translated_title: 间接编码基底中的逐节点激活函数演化：可解性、极限与涌现多样性
translated_abstract: 生物神经元通过特化的细胞类型实现计算多样性：紧张型、爆发型、适应型和快速放电型细胞共存于同一神经回路中。相比之下，人工神经网络对所有节点统一施加单一的激活函数，这限制了它们的表达能力。我们证明这种一致性为演化搜索带来了硬性极限：在稀疏的演化基底上，单调函数无法解决超过其最小实例（即XOR）的奇偶性问题，而单个振荡单元在所有测试规模上都足以解决该问题。这一差距属于搜索与稀疏性问题，而非表达能力问题：单调网络可以用适量的隐藏单元表示奇偶性函数，并且梯度下降能够找到该解。据我们所知，我们首次在间接编码中从包含18种函数的调色板里演化出逐节点的激活函数分配，实验跨越布尔逻辑、回归与稀疏等任务，共计超过4,500次运行（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该研究首次在间接编码中演化逐节点的激活函数分配（从18种函数中选择），并揭示单一激活函数的统一性会给演化搜索带来硬性极限——单调激活函数无法解决超过XOR规模的奇偶性问题，而单个振荡单元即可在任意测试规模下解决。
en_tdlr: This work pioneers per-node activation function evolution in indirect encodings from an 18-function palette, showing that uniform activation functions impose hard limits on evolutionary search—monotonic functions cannot solve parity beyond XOR, while a single oscillatory unit suffices at all tested scales.
